Name: PWDATA[0]
Structural Path: Security propagation chain: PWDATA[0] ⇒ GPIOLOCK write data ⇒ r_gpio_lock[0] ⇒ PADDIR authorization ⇒ gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PWDATA` carries the direction bitmap selected by the lock check immediately before `r_gpio_dir <= pwdata_l`. The relevant dataflow is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PWDATA -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.pwdata_l -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. Once a PADDIR write is admitted, controlling `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.PWDATA` substitutes attacker-selected input/output directions. Pins are configured as outputs or inputs contrary to the authorized software value.
Justification: Selection follows from the reachable propagation chain through PWDATA[0] -> GPIOLOCK write data -> r_gpio_lock[0] -> PADDIR authorization -> gpio_dir: changing or observing PWDATA[0] can affect the protected behavior. Quantitative support is ucp_controllability=0.5, bypass_sensitivity=0.00131234.

Name: r_gpio_lock[0]
Structural Path: Security propagation chain: r_gpio_lock[0] ⇒ PADDIR write authorization ⇒ r_gpio_dir ⇒ gpio_dir
Attack Scenarios: `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock[0]` selects whether `PWDATA` or zero is assigned to `pwdata_l` in the PADDIR case. The relevant dataflow is `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.pwdata_l -> apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.gpio_dir`. On a rising `HCLK`, `r_gpio_dir` is updated only inside `PSEL && PENABLE && PWRITE`, when `s_apb_addr` decodes `REG_PADDIR`; `r_gpio_lock[0] == 0` passes `PWDATA`, otherwise the RTL writes zero. Clearing `apb_gpio_gpio_dir_cone.r_gpio_lock[0]` before the access bypasses the lock and lets attacker-controlled `PWDATA` reach `r_gpio_dir`. The lock policy no longer preserves the authorized pad-direction configuration.
